title: Go inside the Sagrada Familia in the afternoon
description: The western windows are the warm ones. Gaudi started in 1882 and the towers are only now being finished; book a timed entry.

title: Walk the roof terraces of Casa Mila
description: Gaudi's warrior chimneys on an undulating roof with no straight line in it. The night visit includes the rooftop lit up.

title: Find a seat in Park Guell's serpentine bench
description: A failed housing estate turned public park. The monumental zone is ticketed and capped; the woodland above it is free.

title: Eat standing up at the Boqueria before nine
description: The market bars at the back serve breakfast to the stallholders. By eleven it belongs to the tour groups.

title: Walk the ridge above Montserrat monastery
description: A saw-toothed conglomerate massif with a Benedictine monastery halfway up. Take the rack railway and walk down.

title: Follow the Cami de Ronda around the Costa Brava
description: An old coastguard footpath linking coves between Blanes and Portbou. Sant Feliu to Tossa is the stretch to walk.

title: See Dali's own museum at Figueres
description: He designed it, filled it, and is buried under the floor. Easily the strangest major museum in Spain.

title: Walk to the Estany de Sant Maurici
description: Catalonia's only national park: granite peaks, two hundred lakes and no private cars past the gate.

title: Stand in the forest of arches at the Mezquita
description: Eight hundred and fifty columns of a tenth-century mosque with a cathedral dropped into the middle of it. Free entry before nine thirty.

title: Climb the Giralda ramp instead of stairs
description: Thirty-five ramps rather than steps, built so the muezzin could ride a horse to the top of the minaret.

title: See flamenco in a Triana peña
description: The gitano quarter across the river where the form comes from. A peña is a members' club, and most will let you in.

title: Walk the walkways on top of the Setas
description: The largest timber structure in the world, over a Roman excavation. The rooftop walk at sunset costs very little.

title: Look down into the Tajo gorge at Ronda
description: A town split by a hundred-metre gorge and stitched together by an eighteenth-century bridge. Walk down to the bottom for the real view.

title: Walk the Caminito del Rey
description: A metre-wide walkway pinned to a gorge wall a hundred metres up. Rebuilt in 2015 after years as the most dangerous path in Spain.

title: See the sherry bodegas of Jerez
description: The solera system means a glass of fino contains wine from decades of vintages. Tours end in a tasting, as they should.

title: Walk the volcanic coast of Cabo de Gata
description: The driest place in Europe, a protected volcanic coastline of empty beaches and no development. Bring your own water.

title: Look for lynx in Donana
description: Marshland at the mouth of the Guadalquivir holding most of the world's remaining Iberian lynx and half a million wintering birds.

title: Walk up to the Mirador de San Nicolas at sunset
description: The Moorish quarter opposite the Alhambra, and the view across to it as the Sierra Nevada turns pink behind.

title: See Las Meninas in the Prado
description: Velazquez, Goya and Bosch in one building. Free for the last two hours every day, which is exactly when everyone goes.

title: Stand in front of Guernica
description: Picasso would not let it come to Spain until democracy returned. It arrived in 1981 and has not moved since.

title: Eat bocadillo de calamares on the Plaza Mayor
description: A fried squid sandwich in a landlocked city three hundred kilometres from the sea. Madrid does not explain itself.

title: Walk the Retiro at opening time
description: The old royal gardens, with a glasshouse of pure glass and iron and rowing boats on the lake.

title: Walk to La Pedriza above Manzanares
description: A granite badlands of rounded boulders an hour from the city, where Madrid goes climbing at the weekend.

title: Walk under the Segovia aqueduct
description: One hundred and sixty-seven arches of unmortared granite, built around 100 AD and carrying water until the 1970s.

title: Find the frog on the Salamanca facade
description: A small carved frog hidden in the plateresque stonework. Students say finding it unaided means you will pass your exams.

title: See the human fossils at Atapuerca
description: The richest early-human site in Europe, with remains going back 1.2 million years. The dig is open to guided visits.

title: Walk the three-faith quarters of Toledo
description: A synagogue, a mosque and a cathedral within a few hundred metres, in the city where all three coexisted for centuries.

title: See the hanging houses of Cuenca
description: Balconied houses built out over a gorge in the fifteenth century, best seen from the iron footbridge opposite.

title: Stargaze in the Monfrague dark sky reserve
description: A certified starlight reserve that is also the best raptor-watching site in Spain, with black vultures nesting on the Salto del Gitano.

title: Work through the pintxos bars of the Parte Vieja
description: One pintxo and one drink per bar, then move on. The old town has over a hundred and the good ones are standing room only.

title: See the Guggenheim from the river side
description: Gehry's titanium curves turned a dying industrial port around in a decade. The building outside is as much of the point as the art inside.

title: Climb the 241 steps to Gaztelugatxe
description: A hermitage on a rock island joined to the coast by a stone bridge. Free, but you must book a time slot.

title: See the bison at Altamira in the replica cave
description: The first cave art ever recognised as prehistoric, and dismissed as a forgery for twenty years. The neocave reproduces it exactly.

title: Drive up to the Lagos de Covadonga
description: Two glacial lakes at 1,100 metres in the Picos. In summer the road closes to private cars and a shuttle runs instead.

title: Pour Asturian cider from above your head
description: The escanciador pours from arm's length to aerate it, and you drink the small measure straight down. Anything left goes on the floor.

title: Stand at the edge of the Costa da Morte
description: Where the Romans believed the world ended, and where Camino walkers keep going after Santiago to burn their boots.

title: Walk the complete Roman wall at Lugo
description: Two kilometres of third-century wall with a walkway right around the top, the only fully intact Roman circuit anywhere.

title: Take the boat to the Cies Islands
description: A national park with a daily visitor cap and a beach the locals will tell you is the best in the world. Permits book out in July.

title: Walk the route of the encierro when nothing is chasing you
description: Eight hundred and seventy-five metres from the corral to the ring. Doing it on a quiet morning tells you how narrow Estafeta really is.

title: Cycle the badlands of the Bardenas Reales
description: A semi-desert of eroded clay a hundred kilometres from the Pyrenees, with a military bombing range still active in one corner.

title: Walk into the Ordesa canyon
description: A glacial canyon in the high Pyrenees, with the Cola de Caballo waterfall at the head of it. Shuttle bus only in summer.

title: Look for the Mudejar towers of Teruel
description: Brick and glazed-tile towers built by Muslim craftsmen for Christian patrons after the reconquest. Spain's most overlooked provincial capital.

title: Taste in a Rioja bodega built by an architect
description: The Barrio de la Estacion in Haro has the densest concentration of century-old bodegas anywhere, several of them wrapped in modern architecture.

title: Drive the Sa Calobra road
description: Twelve kilometres of hairpins including a full 270-degree loop where the road ties itself in a knot. Cyclists own it at dawn.

title: Walk the dry stone route through the Tramuntana
description: The GR221 links mountain refuges along a world heritage landscape of terraces and olive groves. Spring, before the heat.

title: Walk a stage of the Cami de Cavalls
description: A 185-kilometre bridle path right around Menorca, first cut so mounted patrols could watch for pirates.

title: Watch the sunset over Es Vedra
description: A four-hundred-metre limestone island off the south-west coast, best seen from the cliffs at Cala d'Hort with nothing playing.

title: Watch the stars from Teide
description: Spain's highest point at 3,715 metres, above the cloud layer and inside one of the world's best protected skies. Permits needed for the summit cone.

title: See what Manrique built in the lava
description: A collapsed lava tube turned into a concert hall and pool, with blind albino crabs found nowhere else living in the lagoon.

title: Walk the Ruta de los Volcanes
description: Along the volcanic spine of the island past the 2021 Tajogaite eruption, with both coasts visible most of the way.

title: Walk in the laurel cloud forest of Garajonay
description: A relict forest of the kind that covered the Mediterranean before the ice ages, kept alive by cloud stripping through the trees.

title: Walk the dunes at Corralejo
description: Eleven kilometres of protected white dunes blown in from the Sahara, with Lobos island sitting just offshore.
